findings.title: Fire-and-forget goroutines use parent context that may be canceled before legacy write completes
findings.body: In Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection, the async goroutine does `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` deriving from the request's ctx. Once the HTTP request completes, the original ctx is typically canceled by the server, which will immediately cancel the derived context too, aborting the legacy write before the 10s timeout is reached. This defeats the purpose of "asynchronously write to legacy as a safe measure" since most async legacy writes will likely be canceled right after the response is sent back to the client, silently dropping legacy writes.

findings.title: Metric mislabeled as legacy duration on storage failure
findings.body: In Create, when d.Storage.Create fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` — but this is a storage failure, not a legacy failure. This mislabels the metric, polluting legacy error-duration metrics with storage errors. The same pattern repeats in Update (line ~129) where a storage failure is recorded via `recordLegacyDuration`.

findings.title: Delete records metric using resource name instead of kind
findings.body: `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes `name` (the object's name) where other calls pass `options.Kind`. This produces inconsistent/incorrect metric labels, mixing up object names and resource kinds across metrics, making dashboards for mode3 delete duration unreliable.

findings.title: DeleteCollection records legacy outcome under storage metric
findings.body: In the DeleteCollection async goroutine, after calling d.Legacy.DeleteCollection, the code calls `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`, mislabeling the legacy write duration/outcome as a storage metric.

findings.title: No test coverage for async legacy writes
findings.body: The new tests for Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection only assert the result returned from Storage; they never assert that the legacy store's Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection mocks were actually called (there's no `AssertExpectations`/`AssertCalled` on the legacy mock, and goroutines are fire-and-forget with no synchronization), so the core new behavior of mode 3 — asynchronously writing to legacy as a safety measure — is effectively untested and could silently regress.
